description: i025 complete (SNAPSHOT=s06, branch=peer-trusted-transport). Finding (medium confidence): s06:drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c:204-214 — hdlc_rx_greybus_frame() extracts the peer-controlled 16-bit Greybus header size ("u16 gb_msg_len = le16_to_cpu(gb_frame->hdr.size);" at line 208) from the CC1352 peer MCU's HDLC-framed message over the serdev UART link and delivers it verbatim as the length to greybus_data_rcvd() at line 213, never comparing it to the locally known real frame length (len = bg->rx_buffer_len - 4 computed at gb-beagleplay.c:357 and passed in at line 368 but unused), to the fixed u8 rx_buffer[MAX_RX_HDLC] (~259 bytes, lines 23-25/83), or to any kernel-known maximum; the same driver's TX path enforces a local limit (line 602: le16_to_cpu(msg->header->size) > RX_HDLC_PAYLOAD -> -E2BIG), so the RX mirror omits the check. Downstream gb_connection_recv() (operation.c:1026-1064) re-reads msg_size from the same peer bytes and only tests size < msg_size (vacuous for this caller), and gb_operation_create_incoming() memcpy's the peer-declared size (up to 65535) at operation.c:651 from the small fixed rx_buffer into the heap request message — a peer-triggerable heap OOB read. Counterevidence checked: destination capped by hd->buffer_size_max (operation.c:368-372), response direction capped by locally known message_size (986-992), sibling host driver es2.c:844 is HCI-bounded and safe.
